title: Continual learning for VLA
subtitle: Retaining capabilities while learning new robotic tasks.
summary: Exploring how vision–language–action models can learn sequential manipulation tasks while retaining earlier capabilities, with an interest in experience replay and its storage and training costs.
role: Research participant; research questions and method exploration.
question: Which parts of past experience should a robot reuse when learning a new task?

sections.title: Research context
sections.text: The project considers continual robot learning with the LIBERO simulation environment and the SO-101 robot. Areas of investigation include differences between larger foundation models and lightweight policies, retention of earlier tasks, and the resource costs of replay.

sections.title: My focus
sections.text: I am interested in the relationship between preserving past capabilities and the cost of retaining and revisiting experience. I have also been exploring shared representations with task-specific composition and selective capacity expansion as research hypotheses.

sections.title: Questions under investigation
items: How does experience selection affect learning and retention under a fixed budget?
When can an existing representation be reused for a new task?
How should task success, forgetting, storage, and additional parameters be evaluated together?

cv: Participating in research on sequential VLA learning using LIBERO and SO-101.
Exploring experience reuse, capability retention, and the storage and training costs of replay.

title: Maestro / MobileKT
subtitle: Personalized knowledge tracing on mobile devices.
summary: A team project combining personalized study support with interpretable on-device knowledge tracing. I led the team and worked on the MobileKT model architecture and on-device deployment.
role: Team lead · MobileKT model architecture · on-device deployment.
question: How can a compact model represent a learner’s changing knowledge state?

sections.title: The project
sections.text: Maestro combines quiz generation and knowledge tracing in a mobile study assistant. MobileKT builds on MIKT and uses a content-based question representation and a Time-Aware Probe to estimate concept mastery. The system combines server-side components with on-device knowledge-state updates.

sections.title: My contribution
sections.text: I served as team lead and contributed to the MobileKT architecture and on-device deployment. This connected model design with the practical constraints of integrating a knowledge-tracing component into a mobile application.

sections.title: Reported implementation results
sections.text: The team’s final report records a total size of 1.48 MB for the bundled on-device ONNX models. Across 63 measured steps on a Galaxy Tab S8, the median knowledge-tracing step latency was 49 ms. These figures describe the on-device knowledge-tracing components, not the entire app or server-assisted response time.

sections.title: What I take forward
sections.text: This project informs my interest in persistent state representations, personalization, and the trade-offs between predictive performance, interpretability, and deployment cost. Knowledge-state updates here are distinct from continual updates to model weights.

cv: Team lead; responsible for MobileKT model architecture and on-device deployment.
Team implementation: 1.48 MB of bundled ONNX models; median knowledge-tracing step latency of 49 ms over 63 steps on a Galaxy Tab S8.

title: Edge AI video processing
subtitle: Connecting models to real-time execution constraints.
summary: Model training, conversion, and C++ inference pipelines for object detection and video processing on RK3588 with a DEEPX DX-M1 accelerator.
question: What changes when a vision model has to run in a real system?

sections.title: The system
sections.text: The work connects RTSP video input, image preprocessing, accelerator inference, detection postprocessing, and video recording. The target environment combines an RK3588 single-board computer with the DEEPX DX-M1 accelerator.

sections.title: My contribution
sections.text: I worked on object-detection training and conversion, C++ inference integration, preprocessing and postprocessing, asynchronous execution, and buffer management. Debugging involved checking model input and output formats as well as the behavior of the surrounding pipeline.

sections.title: Research relevance
sections.text: This experience made latency, memory use, and data movement concrete considerations in my work. It informs how I approach the gap between a model’s offline evaluation and its behavior in a deployed system.

cv: Developed object-detection and video-processing components for RK3588 and DEEPX DX-M1.
Worked with C++ asynchronous inference, model conversion, preprocessing, postprocessing, and video input/output.

title: Nano-MemGPT
subtitle: Understanding memory-management failures in small language models.
summary: A research proposal and code scaffold for diagnosing memory-related function-calling failures in small language models and investigating teacher-guided recovery.
question: Does an agent fail because it lacks knowledge, or because it does not retrieve the right memory?

sections.title: The question
sections.text: This work proposes separating answer-generation errors from failures in memory management, such as missing a retrieval call, making an unnecessary call, or stopping a chain of calls too early.

sections.title: Experimental direction
sections.text: The repository provides a scaffold for running Letta/MemGPT baselines, collecting teacher trajectories, diagnosing function-call behavior, and comparing full fine-tuning with LoRA. The intended evaluations include multi-session retrieval and document question answering.

sections.title: Current scope
sections.text: This is a research project in development. The page describes the proposal and experimental setup; it does not claim completed distillation results or verified gains.

cv: Proposed diagnosis of small-model memory-management failures using oracle function calls and failure categories.
Developing an experimental scaffold for teacher trajectories and full fine-tuning / LoRA comparisons.
